title: Composition, Inverses, and Modeling
description: Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first.
outcomes: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.
Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.
Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.
Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.
Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.
Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.
Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.
Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.
Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.
